title: ASF™ trigger — commit-gate (report)
description: What the Commit Gate Agent returns for one commit. The report is advisory: it states a verdict and the actions that would resolve it, and carries no authority to merge, block or write.

action_catalog_version.description: Which catalogue the emitted action codes belong to. A caller that has not implemented this version must say so rather than guess.

status.description: block means at least one entry marked blocks_merge failed. It is a recommendation; the CI or MR rule decides what to do with it.

blocking.description: Ids of the checks that produced the blocking status.

summary.description: One sentence, for a reader in a hurry.

checks.description: One entry per enabled checklist item, in checklist order. Passing entries are reported too: a report that lists only failures cannot be distinguished from a report that ran only some checks.

status.description: not_verifiable means the evidence could not be read — distinct from fail, which means it was read and is wrong. Collapsing the two produces reports that accuse an author of what the agent could not see.

confidence.description: A judgement made on a partial diff is worth less than one made on a complete diff, and the reader is entitled to know which this is.

items.description: Flat, severity-ordered list of everything found wrong, each with somewhere to jump to. This is the navigable list a console renders.

next_best_actions.description: Ranked across the whole report, so that 'what to do next' is rank 1 and not a judgement left to the reader. Every entry is a catalogue code with its parameters filled: the caller dispatches it without parsing prose.

code.description: A code from the Action Catalogue. The agent selects; it never invents. An unknown code is a caller-side error, not an instruction to improvise.

parameters.description: Filled according to the catalogue entry's parameter schema. Every required property must be present, or the action is not emittable and the agent must say why instead.

label.description: The same action in one imperative line, for a human. Derived from the code, never a substitute for it.

executor.description: Who would carry it out. This agent never does: it names the executor and stops. The separation is what keeps the verdict independent of the remedy.

not_verifiable.description: What could not be looked at, and why. Reported explicitly so that a silent gap is never read as a pass.
